skill.name: fit-scorer
skill.description: Use when the user asks to "score this influencer", "rank these creators for our campaign", or "tell me which influencer is the best fit"; produces weighted fit scores across audience match, content quality, brand alignment, engagement authenticity, and partnership potential, plus a ranked comparison and a go/pass verdict. Not for finding new influencers — use influencer-discovery; not for sending outreach — use outreach-manager.
skill.summary: Scores and ranks shortlisted influencers using weighted campaign-fit criteria and clear go or pass recommendations.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, and relative documentation links. One command-execution finding is confirmed because the skill directs an agent to run a Python connector with a user-provided handle without explicit argument validation. The skill also persists campaign and creator assessments to shared memory paths, creating a privacy and retention concern.

remediation.issue: The YouTube connector command accepts a creator handle without documented validation or shell-safety requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Validate handles against a strict platform format, pass arguments without shell interpolation, and request confirmation before running the networked connector.

remediation.issue: Campaign context, creator assessments, rankings, and verdicts are automatically written to persistent shared memory files.
remediation.suggestion: Request consent before persistence, minimize stored data, avoid shared hot-cache promotion by default, and document deletion and retention controls.

content.user_title: Score and Rank Influencers for Campaign Fit
content.value_statement: Choosing creators by instinct can waste campaign budget and hide selection risks. This skill applies weighted criteria and produces comparable scores with clear recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Scores audience match, content quality, brand alignment, engagement quality, and partnership potential.
Adjusts dimension weights for awareness, engagement, conversion, brand-building, or long-term campaign goals.
Applies follower authenticity, brand safety, and engagement authenticity veto checks before ranking.
Compares multiple creators with dimension-level scores, weighted totals, rankings, and go or pass verdicts.
Uses user-provided evidence or measured YouTube metrics when the optional connector is available.
Produces structured reports with strengths, concerns, expected performance, and recommended campaign roles.
limitations: It does not discover new influencers or send outreach messages.
Scores depend on the accuracy and completeness of supplied metrics and creator evidence.
The optional YouTube connector requires an API key and command execution.
The framework cannot guarantee campaign performance, pricing, availability, or future creator behavior.

use_cases.title: Prioritize a campaign shortlist
use_cases.description: Rank several creators using one consistent framework and identify the strongest candidate for a defined campaign goal.

use_cases.title: Defend creator selection
use_cases.description: Create a documented scorecard that explains audience fit, brand alignment, authenticity, risks, and the final recommendation.

use_cases.title: Review partnership candidates
use_cases.description: Compare creator history, professionalism, value, availability, and audience quality before committing budget or negotiating terms.

prompt_templates.title: Score one creator
prompt_templates.prompt: Score @[handle] for [brand or campaign]. Use the default weights, explain each dimension, and provide a go or pass verdict.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one shortlisted influencer

prompt_templates.title: Rank a shortlist
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare and rank [creator handles] for [campaign]. The goal is [goal], and the target audience is [audience]. Show weighted scores and concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Apply conversion weighting
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [creator handles] for a conversion campaign. Prioritize audience match, verify engagement authenticity, apply veto checks, and recommend the best campaign role.

prompt_templates.title: Build an evidence-based partner portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Score [creator handles] using these custom weights: [weights]. Separate measured facts from estimates, identify evidence gaps, apply vetoes, and recommend priority, backup, and pass tiers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced portfolio decision with custom weighting

output_examples.input: Score @northstarcreator for a sustainable skincare awareness campaign targeting United States adults aged 25 to 40.
output_examples.output: Final score: 4.1 out of 5, Recommended. Strong audience and content fit support awareness goals. Verify follower authenticity before contracting.

output_examples.input: Rank @creatorA, @creatorB, and @creatorC for a conversion campaign using the available audience and engagement data.
output: 1. @creatorB: 4.4 out of 5, Highly Recommended for conversion.
2. @creatorA: 3.8 out of 5, Recommended with pricing concerns.
3. @creatorC: 2.9 out of 5, Pass because engagement authenticity needs verification.

output_examples.input: Compare two creators when audience demographics are incomplete.
output_examples.output: The report scores supported dimensions, marks audience estimates as unverified, lists missing evidence, and gives a provisional ranking with reduced confidence.

best_practices: Use the same evidence window and scoring definitions for every creator in a comparison.
Label measured data, user-provided facts, estimates, and missing evidence separately.
Review veto evidence and high scores manually before outreach or budget approval.
anti_patterns: Do not invent demographics, engagement metrics, partnership history, rates, or availability.
Do not compare creators using different weights or evidence periods without explaining the difference.
Do not treat a weighted score as a guarantee of sales, safety, or partnership success.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the campaign goal, target audience, brand values, creator handles, relevant metrics, content examples, and known partnership history.

faq.question: Can it score one influencer?
faq.answer: Yes. It produces dimension scores, a weighted total, key strengths, concerns, and a clear recommendation.

faq.question: Can it compare creators across platforms?
faq.answer: Yes, when comparable evidence is available. Platform-specific metrics should be normalized and their limitations stated.

faq.question: Does it require a connector?
faq.answer: No. It can score user-provided information, while the optional YouTube connector can supply measured engagement inputs.

faq.question: How are campaign goals reflected?
faq.answer: The skill changes dimension weights for awareness, engagement, conversion, brand building, or long-term partnership goals.

faq.question: Does the score guarantee campaign results?
faq.answer: No. The score supports comparison and documentation, but performance still depends on creative execution, pricing, timing, and external conditions.
